newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 closes down in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 closes down in quiet trading.

text.p: 1400 GMT - The Czech PX50 closes lower in thin trading on Friday.
174 shares on bourse rise, 193 fall, 117 unchanged.
The Czech PX50 index fell back sharply on Friday led by its most heavily weighted share, SPT Telecom.

SPT dropped 134 crowns, 3.9 percent, to 3,301 pulling the PX50 down 1.3 percent to 543.4. But dealers said the decline was more a reflection of lack of demand in the Czech market as a whole rather than fundamental problems with SPT.
"I don't think it is a problem with SPT fundamentally. I just think this is a reflection of what's going on in the market," said Ivan Kusacek of Zivnostenska Banka.

Kusacek said measures to reform the capital markets announced by the government on Wednesday would help shares only in the long term and stressed that confidence in the Czech market would take much longer to restore than it took to be lost.

While the PX50 surged in anticipation of the announcement, which will attempt to make market prices more realistic, stamp out corruption in investment funds, and more tightly regulate the market generally, it has fallen back since.
